name: The Group's code lives where its section names what it does, once, in standard forms
asks:
[2026-09-21] it feels like so much of this would be solved if, once again: we used norms and standards to store things, this would be easy. if eavt stuff was all under an eavt-engineering-services-section ... HOLY SHIT CONSOLIDATE

[2026-09-22] Literally just look at the funciton and if it does what the directory says, it goes there, and if not, it doesn't. ... ANd bulk moving things isn't helpful, when the code itself is misconstructed, and we still end up with like 400 different implementations of the same code. ... We designed our software to mimick, even in name, standard known software. "Does it go in FeltOS?" "Well, would it go in FluffOS?"

[2026-09-26] MARSH is literally meant to be what puts that stuff onto EVM, it's meant to be our EVM library ... (This is similar to how LAGOON is meant to be what puts our stuff into Guix/Guile, with effectful stuff being in Node.)

[2026-10-08] Look for data bloat and drift, like where we store shit in stupid reundant ways, handwrite json without readers, and so on

met-when.command: sh -c 'for t in feltos lagoon marsh; do test -f lib/emsenn/services/561-group/services/engineering-services-section/content/text/glossary/terms/$t.md || exit 1; done'

x-provenance.recorded-by: Red Cup Engineer Senior (development pass signstuff-substrate of debt-2026-10-09-leader-words-held-in-corpus)
x-provenance.basis: The Leader's utterances to the Group's agents, read from the leader-utterances record in the emsenn section. The asks field quotes them; the requirements are their EARS rendering and carry no scope the words do not.

board-opening.need: Every function and data class of the Group's code sits, once, in the package whose section names what it does, storing data in standard forms, so repair reduces the code's size and divergence.

requirements.says: Each function and data class of the Group's code shall live in the package whose section names what it does.
requirements.rationale: The Leader, 2026-09-22: "Literally just look at the funciton and if it does what the directory says, it goes there, and if not, it doesn't."

requirements.says: Each capability of the Group's code shall have one implementation.
requirements.rationale: The Leader, 2026-09-22: "we still end up with like 400 different implementations of the same code"; 2026-09-21: "HOLY SHIT CONSOLIDATE".

requirements.says: The Group's code shall store data in standard formats and the house's specializations of them.
requirements.rationale: The Leader, 2026-09-21: "if, once again: we used norms and standards to store things, this would be easy."

requirements.says: The Group's EAVT capabilities shall live in the EAVT section under JSONL engineering (eavt-services-section).
requirements.rationale: The Leader, 2026-09-21: "if eavt stuff was all under an eavt-engineering-services-section".

requirements.says: Each Group software package shall take the scope of the standard known software its name mimics.
requirements.rationale: The Leader, 2026-09-22: "We designed our software to mimick, even in name, standard known software. 'Does it go in FeltOS?' 'Well, would it go in FluffOS?'"

requirements.says: The Group's code shall decrease in size, complexity and divergence of implementations with each repair.
requirements.rationale: The Leader, 2026-09-22: repair since mid-April "is taking like, literally 8x more effort than writing the code, and STILL hasn't demosntratably fixed anything"; the measure is "reducing the size, complexity, divergence of implementations".

requirements.says: The Group's data shall be stored in one form, without redundant copies of the same facts.
requirements.rationale: The Leader, 2026-10-08: "Look for data bloat and drift, like where we store shit in stupid reundant ways, handwrite json without readers".

requirements.says: The git services section shall provide git codecs and basic git tooling, and no capability outside them.
requirements.rationale: The Leader, 2026-09-23: git-services-section "extends far past 'codecs for git' and yet also fails to provide even basic git tooling".

requirements.says: FeltOS shall carry the Group's code-fabrication library modules.
requirements.rationale: The Leader, 2026-09-23: "find the one useful function buried in that package, and extract it into our feltos library modules for doing code fabrication".

requirements.says: FeltOS shall add the web platform and persistence to disk to the agent organization engine, which stays a library.
requirements.rationale: The Leader, 2026-09-22: "FeltOS, which is basically what takes our agentic-relation-engine and adds in web-platform and the stuff that lets it persist to disc, whereas agentic-relation-engine is meant more to be a library."

requirements.says: MARSH shall run the Group's operations on-chain on the EVM.
requirements.rationale: The Leader, 2026-09-26: "MARSH is literally meant to be what puts that stuff onto EVM, it's meant to be our EVM library".

requirements.says: MARSH shall reach effects off-chain only through other Group packages.
requirements.rationale: The Leader, 2026-09-26: "It should use other packages to have effects off-chain, when necessary, but otherwise should be entirely EVM."

requirements.says: LAGOON shall put the Group's software into Guix and Guile.
requirements.rationale: The Leader, 2026-09-26: "LAGOON is meant to be what puts our stuff into Guix/Guile".

requirements.says: LAGOON shall run its effectful work in Node.
requirements.rationale: The Leader, 2026-09-26: "with effectful stuff being in Node".

requirements.says: The Group's web server shall serve semantic hypertext packets.
requirements.rationale: The Leader, 2026-09-22: "semantic-hypertext-packet is a thing that our web-server is meant to serve, and what our web-applications and web-platform are meant to communicate in".

requirements.says: The Group's web applications and web platform shall communicate in semantic hypertext packets.

conditions.says: A census of the computer-engineering tree lists each capability with its one owning package.
No EAVT row codec exists outside the EAVT section.
Each brand term in the engineering glossary names the standard software it mimics.
Each data/records form has one reader and no duplicate form.
The git services section's exports are git codecs and git tooling only.
The FeltOS, MARSH and LAGOON packages hold only the capabilities R9–R14 give them.
The web server's responses and the web platform's messages are semantic hypertext packets.

board-opening.context: Specification note: engineering-services-section/content/text/documents/articles/notes/2026/10/10/2026-10-10-note-on-placing-code-by-what-it-does.md, which also records the state on 2026-10-10 of each path the Leader named.
